rubric_items.reason: All eight known REQs in the intent are traced. S-1 traces REQ-1 to REQ-5 and REQ-8. S-2 traces REQ-6 and REQ-7. Nothing is assumed or unknown.
There are two stories, and each has one user-facing outcome: see the count, and open the list behind it. S-2 depends on S-1, because the count must exist before anyone can select it.

The criteria are Given/When/Then and can be checked against the dashboard tile rule. In the body, S-2 AC2 has no When clause, and S-1 AC2 sets up a No-show after today, which the baseline does not allow.
Every value comes from the intent: the label, the 30-day window, Asia/Kolkata, the dashboard tile rule, 0 and the list filters. No new limits are added.
The stories read clearly and use glossary terms. The prose body abbreviates some criteria, so it drifts from the YAML wording in places.

findings.text: S-1 AC2 in the body sets up No-shows that start after the end of today. The intent says No-show is allowed only after the start time, so this setup cannot happen. The YAML version correctly says 'an appointment' instead.

cites.quote: Given No-shows outside the window (before it, or after the end of today in Asia/Kolkata)
`No-show` is allowed only after the start time, and No-show appointments never change.

findings.suggested_fix: Match the body to the YAML: a No-show before the window, and any appointment starting after the end of today.

findings.text: S-2 AC2 in the body has no When clause, so it does not follow Given/When/Then. The YAML version has one ('when staff look at it').

cites.quote: AC2: Given that list, then the number of appointments listed equals the count.

findings.suggested_fix: Add 'when staff look at it' so the body matches the YAML criterion.

findings.text: S-2 cannot be delivered or tested without S-1, because its Given needs the count that S-1 adds. The artifact does not state this dependency or the order of the stories.

findings.suggested_fix: Say that S-2 depends on S-1 and must ship after it.
